title: Blower Motor Won't Turn On? What to Check First
h1: Why Won't My HVAC Blower Motor Turn On, and What Do Pros Check First?
description: If your HVAC blower won't turn on, start with the thermostat, breaker, filter and furnace door switch. Then learn the two tests technicians run next.
quick_answer: A blower that won't run is usually caused by something simple: a thermostat setting, a tripped breaker, a loose furnace door switch, a full condensate safety switch, or an overheated motor tripped by a clogged filter. If those check out, a technician will typically test the run capacitor and the control board relay before replacing the motor.
body:
What does the blower motor do?

The blower is the fan inside your furnace or air handler. It pulls air through the return and filter, pushes it across the heat exchanger or AC coil, and sends it out through the ducts. When it stops, the heating or cooling may still be running, but nothing reaches the rooms.

In most Southern California homes the blower sits inside a furnace in the attic, garage or a hall closet. It's the part you hear spin up a minute or so after the thermostat calls.

What can you safely check yourself?

Start here before calling anyone. None of these steps involve opening electrical compartments.

  1. Thermostat. Make sure it's set to Heat or Cool and the setpoint is above or below room temperature. Switch the fan from Auto to On. If the blower starts, the motor works and the issue is elsewhere in the call for heat or cooling. Replace thermostat batteries if it has them.
  2. Breaker and service switch. Check the breaker panel for a tripped breaker labeled furnace or air handler. Near the furnace there's usually a switch that looks like a light switch. Make sure it's on.
  3. Furnace door. Furnaces have a safety switch that cuts power when the blower door is off or loose. Make sure the panel is seated firmly.
  4. Air filter. A badly clogged filter can make the motor overheat and shut off on its internal protection. Replace it, wait 30 minutes and try again.
  5. Condensate safety switch. Attic systems often have a float switch in the drain pan or drain line. If the line clogs and water backs up, the switch shuts the system down. Water in the pan is a clue.

If you smell gas at any point, stop, leave the house and call the gas utility from outside. Don't flip switches or reset anything.

What are the two tests pros run first?

When the basics check out, technicians usually go straight to two components before condemning the motor. These involve live high-voltage circuits and stored electrical charge, so they're jobs for a trained tech, not a homeowner.

1. The run capacitor

Many blower motors use a capacitor to give them the push to start and keep running. Capacitors weaken with age and heat, and attic temperatures in summer are hard on them. A failing capacitor can leave the motor humming without spinning, starting slowly, or not starting at all. The tech discharges it safely and measures it against its rating. It's a common and fairly simple repair.

2. The control board relay

The furnace control board has a relay that sends power to the blower when the thermostat calls. If the relay sticks or the board fails, the motor never gets power. The tech checks whether voltage is reaching the motor when it should. If it is and the motor still won't run, the motor is the likely problem. If it isn't, the board or wiring is.

What if the motor itself has failed?

Signs of a failed motor include a burning smell, a seized shaft that won't turn by hand with the power off, or a motor that runs briefly and then shuts off hot. Newer systems often use variable-speed ECM motors with their own electronics module, which are tested differently and sometimes repaired by replacing just the module.

Whether to replace the motor or the whole system depends on the age and condition of the equipment. A technician can walk you through that honestly.

When should you call for service?

  • The blower hums but doesn't spin
  • You smell burning or see scorch marks
  • The breaker trips again after you reset it
  • The fan works on On but not during a heating or cooling call
  • The system shuts off with water in the drain pan

Our HVAC repair technicians diagnose blower problems across San Diego and Orange County, and we'll show you what failed before replacing anything.
faqs: Why is my blower motor humming but not spinning?

Humming with no movement often points to a failed run capacitor or a seized motor bearing. Turn the system off so the motor does not overheat, and call for service. Capacitors hold a charge even with the power off, so leave testing and replacement to a technician.
Can a dirty filter stop the blower motor?

Yes. A badly clogged filter starves the motor of air, and the motor can overheat and shut itself off on internal protection. Replace the filter, give the motor time to cool, then try again. If it keeps shutting off, have the system checked.
Why does my AC run outside but no air comes out of the vents?

If the outdoor unit runs but the indoor blower does not, the coil can freeze up. Turn the system off at the thermostat and call for service. Common causes include a failed blower capacitor, motor, control board or a tripped safety switch.
How long do blower motors last?

It varies with the motor type, how often it runs, filter habits and how hot the space around it gets. A motor in a hot attic with dirty filters works harder than one in a clean, cool closet. Regular maintenance helps it last longer.
